---
name: writing-skills
description: Use when creating or editing skills and choosing proportionate validation before installation.
---

# Writing Skills

Write the shortest guidance that changes a useful decision. Prefer a clear
trigger, desired outcome, relevant source, and actual authority boundary.
Leave implementation choices to the model. Remove contradictory instructions,
repeated rules, pressure language, and rituals instead of adding exceptions.

Use the established canonical source and installation path. Keep the skill
entrypoint small; put specialized detail in references loaded only when needed.
Preserve unrelated settings and user instructions when updating runtime mirrors.

At the end, choose validation that could detect the actual defect: metadata and
link checks for structure, existing deterministic tests for helper behavior,
and a few realistic scenarios for a significant decision change. Evaluate
what the agent should do, not whether it repeats a required sentence.
Do not require authenticated model calls when a deterministic contract test
or scenario inspection establishes the change. A separate agent evaluation is
optional when its expected confidence justifies latency and cost; it is not a
prerequisite for writing the skill. No automatic RED/GREEN pressure cycle.

Report changed behavior, evidence actually obtained, and any material limits.
Do not claim static validation proves future model behavior or measured speed.
